notes.title: VoxAging: Continuously Tracking Speaker Aging with a Large-Scale Longitudinal Dataset in English and Mandarin
notes.bp: A speaker system should recognize that a person's voice changes with age rather than treating time-varying identity as noise.
notes.wh: Longitudinal recordings mix biological change, channel variation, language, and recording history.
notes.naive: Train one speaker model on pooled recordings and assume a speaker embedding remains stationary.
notes.ap: Build a longitudinal English/Mandarin resource and measure how aging changes verification evidence.
notes.mech: Link recordings across years, then test verification as time gap, age group, and gender change.
notes.math: EER and embedding cosine similarity turn identity preservation into separability and distance between same-speaker observations.
notes.eval: VoxAging contains 293 speakers with spans up to about 17 years; verification is evaluated with EER and cosine similarity, comparing ECAPA and ERes2Net systems.
notes.ww: The paper reports declining verification accuracy and embedding similarity as recordings move farther apart in time, with age and gender affecting the rate of change.
notes.po: The paper's payoff is a more explicit account of age-and-development; the reported benefit remains author-reported.
notes.limits: Speaker coverage, language balance, recording channels, gated data, and longitudinal confounding limit causal claims about biological aging.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: Patient-Aware Feature Alignment for Robust Lung Sound Classification: Cohesion-Separation and Global Alignment Losses
notes.bp: A clinical audio classifier should distinguish medically meaningful lung-sound patterns without letting patient identity dominate.
notes.wh: Patient-specific acoustics and recording conditions can make a classifier memorize who was recorded instead of pathology.
notes.naive: Optimize ordinary cross-entropy on pooled recordings and trust aggregate accuracy.
notes.ap: Align patient-aware representations while separating normal and abnormal acoustic evidence.
notes.mech: Combine pretrained audio features with patient-aware alignment, cohesion-separation, and global-alignment losses before classification.
notes.math: Similarity and separation losses reshape within-patient and across-class distances; sensitivity, specificity, and ICBHI score expose different errors.
notes.eval: The ICBHI 2017 corpus has 6,898 recordings and an official 60/40 split; five-run comparisons report sensitivity, specificity, and ICBHI score with backbone and loss ablations.
notes.ww: The paper reports improved ICBHI performance and more patient-balanced behavior with the proposed alignment losses.
notes.po: The paper's payoff is a more explicit account of clinical-speech-marker; the reported benefit remains author-reported.
notes.limits: Patient/device distribution, benchmark labels, acoustic conditions, and absent clinical deployment evaluation limit medical interpretation.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: Enabling the replicability of speech synthesis perceptual evaluations
notes.bp: A speech-synthesis listening claim should be inspectable and repeatable, not just summarized by one MOS number.
notes.wh: Subjective results depend on stimuli, participants, protocol, anchors, randomization, analysis, and reporting choices.
notes.naive: Report a mean listener score and assume reproducibility because the model and samples are named.
notes.ap: Decompose evaluation into a structured report and a recipe containing materials and decisions needed to repeat it.
notes.mech: Audit the goal, dataset and bias, participant cohort, protocol, analysis, conclusions, and limitations, then package evaluation assets and procedures.
notes.math: The central object is an auditable mapping from hypothesis to stimuli, ratings, uncertainty, and conclusion.
notes.eval: This protocol paper contributes a checklist, evaluation-report structure, and reproducibility recipe rather than a new held-out model benchmark.
notes.ww: The paper reports a structured template intended to make subjective speech-synthesis studies more reproducible and limitations more visible.
notes.po: The paper's payoff is a more explicit account of auditability-and-contestability; the reported benefit remains author-reported.
notes.limits: A checklist cannot guarantee participant representativeness, perceptual validity, or exact replication when access differs.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: FoleyMaster: High-Quality Video-to-Audio Synthesis via MLLM-Augmented Prompt Tuning and Joint Semantic-Temporal Adaptation
notes.bp: Video-to-audio generation must produce sound that matches what happens in a video and when it happens.
notes.wh: A generated sound can be semantically plausible but mistimed, or aligned but acoustically unrelated.
notes.naive: Prompt a generic text-to-audio model with a caption and ignore fine-grained event timing.
notes.ap: Use MLLM-augmented prompting and semantic-temporal adaptation for event identity and onset structure.
notes.mech: Video semantics guide the prompt while probabilistic temporal conditioning aligns generated events with visual onsets.
notes.math: CLIP score measures semantic alignment and onset accuracy measures temporal agreement; their separation exposes two failures.
notes.eval: FoleyMaster is evaluated on VGGSound Plus with CLIP Score and onset accuracy, baselines, ablations, and a 20-participant pairwise study.
notes.ww: The paper reports gains across semantic and temporal metrics and user preference, with prompt/time components supported by ablations.
notes.po: The paper's payoff is a more explicit account of intelligibility-naturalness; the reported benefit remains author-reported.
notes.limits: Automatic proxies, dataset distribution, event taxonomy, and a small listener study limit claims about real-world Foley usefulness.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: CLAP-ART: Automated Audio Captioning with Semantic-rich Audio Representation Tokenizer
notes.bp: An audio caption should identify the sound event a listener treats as the referent, not merely match common caption words.
notes.wh: Caption metrics reward n-gram overlap while missing semantic adequacy, and discrete representations can discard event details.
notes.naive: Feed a generic continuous audio embedding to a caption decoder and optimize only caption likelihood.
notes.ap: Use a semantic-rich audio representation tokenizer with multi-layer codebooks.
notes.mech: CLAP-ART converts audio into discrete representations learned from semantic audio features; a caption model conditions on those tokens.
notes.math: CIDEr, SPICE, and SPIDEr compare generated language with references, but each is only a proxy for grounded event meaning.
notes.eval: CLAP-ART is tested on AudioCaps and a second audio-caption benchmark with BLEU, METEOR, ROUGE-L, CIDEr, SPICE, and SPIDEr, including six-run averages and codebook ablations.
notes.ww: The paper reports improved caption scores and a favorable multi-layer codebook tradeoff.
notes.po: The paper's payoff is a more explicit account of referential-grounding; the reported benefit remains author-reported.
notes.limits: Reference-caption variability, language bias, metric disagreement, and no independent human grounding study limit claims.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: Direct-path Relative Harmonic Coefficients Detection for Multi-source Direction-of-Arrival Estimation in Reverberant Environments
notes.bp: A microphone array should locate several sources even when reverberation hides the direct path.
notes.wh: Reflections create false direction evidence and make direct-path bins sparse or unstable.
notes.naive: Search the whole spatial grid with a conventional beamformer or treat every bin as equally reliable.
notes.ap: Detect direct-path relative harmonic coefficients and use reliable spatial evidence for 3D localization.
notes.mech: Estimate relative harmonic structure, identify valid direct-path bins, and aggregate their directional evidence.
notes.math: Mean absolute angular error measures localization distance; valid-bin proportion measures whether usable spatial observations were found.
notes.eval: Simulated reverberant scenes vary source count and T60, with recorded conditions also tested; MAEE and valid-bin proportion compare four baselines.
notes.ww: The paper reports lower localization error in most tested reverberant scenarios and improved robustness.
notes.po: The paper's payoff is a more explicit account of spatial-filtering; the reported benefit remains author-reported.
notes.limits: Array geometry, source count, room conditions, harmonic assumptions, and angular-error averaging limit transfer.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: Accessible Real-time Eye-gaze Tracking for Neurocognitive Health Assessment: A Multimodal Web-based Approach
notes.bp: A real-time eye-gaze health tool should be usable by people with different motor and cognitive profiles, not only accurate for an average user.
notes.wh: Gaze error, fatigue, engagement, task difficulty, and individual movement interact, so one accuracy score misses usability.
notes.naive: Train one gaze predictor and evaluate only aggregate spatial error.
notes.ap: Combine accessible web-based interaction with task-specific metric families, cohort analysis, classification, and usability feedback.
notes.mech: Extract distance, velocity, saccade, and task metrics, compare cohorts, and use selected features in an AdaBoost classifier.
notes.math: Feature selection and cross-validation turn gaze traces into a cohort-level decision, while survey ratings expose usability beyond classifier accuracy.
notes.eval: Kruskal-Wallis selection, k-fold validation, accuracy/F1, and survey ratings connect gaze traces to cohort decisions.
notes.ww: The paper reports AdaBoost at 0.89 accuracy and 0.67 F1 against 0.77 baseline, plus a 39-participant usability survey with 82% high engagement.
notes.po: The paper's payoff is a more explicit account of accessibility-fit; the reported benefit remains author-reported.
notes.limits: Cohort composition, task design, leakage risk, self-report, and absent clinical validation limit health claims.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: Mitigating Audiovisual Mismatch in Visual-Guide Audio Captioning
notes.bp: Visual-guide audio captioning should remain semantically faithful when audio and visual streams do not line up.
notes.wh: Audiovisual mismatch can make a model overtrust the wrong modality and describe the wrong event fluently.
notes.naive: Train on perfectly synchronized pairs and assume test alignment is identical.
notes.ap: Use systematic audiovisual shuffling and semantic/temporal adaptation to train and test under mismatch.
notes.mech: Vary shuffle probability while semantic and temporal modules preserve event meaning and timing.
notes.math: Caption metrics combine n-gram and semantic measures; repeated timed inference exposes accuracy and deployment cost.
notes.eval: The paper evaluates eight caption metrics across shuffle probabilities, ablates semantic/temporal components, varies video length, and averages timed inference.
notes.ww: The paper reports stronger semantic resilience under mismatch, with both modules contributing.
notes.po: The paper's payoff is a more explicit account of referential-grounding; the reported benefit remains author-reported.
notes.limits: Synthetic shuffle may not represent real errors; caption variability and proxy metrics limit human-grounding claims.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.
